title: Synthesis of Strong Adhesive Hydrogel, Gelatin O-Nitrosobenzaldehyde
protocol: Add 9.4 g of methyl 4-(4-formyl-2-methoxyphenoxy) butanoate slowly to a precooled (-2 °C) solution of 70% nitric acid and stir at -2 °C for 3 h.
Filter the mixture with 200 mL of 0 °C water.
Hydrolyze the solid product in trifluoroacetic acid (TFA)/H2O, 1:10 v/v at 90 °C.
Dry and remove the solvent under vacuum to obtain a dry pale-yellow powder intermediate product.
Dissolve the intermediate product in tetrahydrofuran (THF)/ethanol, 1:1 v/v.
Add NaBH4 slowly at 0 °C and stir for 3 h.
Remove all solvents under vacuum and suspend the residue in a 1:1 water and dichloromethane solution.
Extract the product from the aqueous layer using dichloromethane.
Dry the organic layer over magnesium sulfate.
Purify the crude product by silica gel column chromatography using DCM/MeOH at a 10:1 ratio (1% TEA).
Obtain relatively pure yellowish powder NB-COOH.
Prepare a homogeneous gelatin solution by dissolving 5 g of gelatin in 100 mL of deionized water and store at 37 °C.
Dissolve 1,060 mg of NB-COOH in 5 mL of dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Add 746 mg of EDC into the NB-COOH DMSO solution and stir for 5 min.
After EDC has dissolved, add 448 mg of NHS and stir for 5 min.
Use a dropping funnel to slowly drop the mixture at a rate of 0.5 mL/min into the dissolved gelatin solution with vigorous stirring to react at 45 °C for 4 h.
Dialyze the gelatin-NB solution against excess deionized water for at least 3 days.
Collect, freeze, and lyophilize the dialyzed gelatin-NB solution to obtain foams.
Keep the foams in a desiccator in the dark for further use.
Dissolve the freeze-dried gelatin-NB foams in deionized water at 37 °C immediately before use.
